title: Isaiah's Call
summary: In the year King Uzziah dies Isaiah sees the Lord on a high throne, with the train of his robe filling the temple and seraphim crying 'Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts.' Isaiah cries out that he is a man of unclean lips. A seraph touches his lips with a live coal from the altar and says his guilt is taken away. Isaiah answers 'Here am I; send me' and is told to go to a people who hear but do not understand, until cities lie waste.

title: Ahaz and the Sign of Immanuel
summary: When Rezin of Syria and Pekah of Israel threaten Judah, King Ahaz and his people shake like trees in the wind. The LORD sends Isaiah with his son Shear-jashub to tell Ahaz to be calm. Ahaz declines to ask for a sign, saying he will not tempt the LORD, and Isaiah says the LORD himself will give one: a virgin, a word whose Hebrew is debated, will conceive and bear a son called Immanuel. Before he knows good from evil the two kings' lands will be forsaken, and Assyria will come.

title: Sennacherib's Threat and Hezekiah
summary: Sennacherib's field commander stands before Jerusalem and mocks Hezekiah's trust in Egypt and in the LORD, speaking in Hebrew so the people on the wall can hear. Hezekiah tears his clothes, sends to Isaiah, and then spreads Sennacherib's letter before the LORD and prays. Isaiah says the king of Assyria will not enter the city or shoot an arrow there. That night the angel of the LORD strikes 185,000 in the Assyrian camp, and Sennacherib goes home, where his sons kill him in a temple.

title: Hezekiah's Illness
summary: Hezekiah falls ill, and Isaiah tells him to set his house in order because he will die. Hezekiah turns his face to the wall, weeps and prays, and Isaiah brings word that God will add fifteen years, deliver the city from Assyria, and make the shadow on the dial go back ten degrees. Hezekiah writes a song of thanks. When envoys from Merodach-baladan of Babylon arrive with letters and a gift, he shows them all his treasures, and Isaiah says it will all be carried to Babylon.
